### What “CPU usage” actually means * **CPU usage** is a measure of how busy your processor(s) are at any given moment. * It’s usually expressed as a percentage of the total processing capacity available. * 0 % → the CPU is completely idle. * 100 % → all cores are fully occupied (or one core is saturated if you’re looking at a single‑core view). * Modern operating systems report two kinds of CPU usage: * **System‑wide** – the aggregate load across all cores. * **Per‑process** – how much of the CPU time each running program is consuming. --- ## How to look at CPU usage on different platforms | Platform | Quick GUI tool | Command‑line / script | |----------|----------------|-----------------------| | **Windows** | **Task Manager** (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) → Performance tab → CPU graph. | `wmic cpu get loadpercentage`
`Get-Counter '\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time'` (PowerShell)
`typeperf "\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time" -si 1 -sc 10` (cmd) | | **Linux** | `htop` (interactive, color‑coded). | `top` (press `1` to see per‑core stats).
`mpstat -P ALL 1 5` (requires sysstat).
`vmstat 1 5` (shows idle, system, etc.). | | **macOS** | **Activity Monitor** → CPU tab. | `top -l 1 -n 0` (single snapshot).
`ps -A -o %cpu,%mem,comm` (per‑process). | > **Tip:** On Windows, you can also open **Resource Monitor** (`resmon`) for more detailed per‑process breakdowns. --- ## Interpreting the numbers | Column | Meaning | Typical threshold | |--------|---------|-------------------| | `%CPU` (or `CPU%`) | Percentage of CPU time used by a process or overall. | < 20 % → normal idle.
20–50 % → moderate load.
> 80 % → heavy load; may indicate a runaway process or a demanding workload. | | `%MEM` | Memory usage as a percentage of physical RAM. | > 70 % → memory pressure; may cause swapping. | | `Idle` (Linux `idle` column) | Time spent not doing useful work. | > 90 % → system is mostly idle. | | `iowait` (Linux `wa` column) | Time waiting for I/O. | > 5 % → disk bottleneck. | > **Remember:** A single process can show a high %CPU even if the overall system is still under 30 % because it may be a multi‑threaded application that uses many cores. --- ## Common scenarios where CPU spikes happen | Cause | What to look for | Fix / mitigation | |-------|------------------|------------------| | Background services (e.g., Windows Update, antivirus scans) | Look for `svchost.exe`, `wuauserv`, `MsMpEng.exe`. | Disable or schedule during off‑hours. | | Malware / cryptomining | Unusual processes with high CPU and no obvious UI. | Run full AV scan, check Task Scheduler for hidden tasks. | | System updates / drivers | Kernel threads (`kworker`, `ntoskrnl.exe`). | Wait for completion, update drivers. | | Heavy workloads (video rendering, compiling, gaming) | Dedicated apps (`ffmpeg`, `gcc`, game executables). | Acceptable; consider throttling or upgrading hardware. | | Thermal throttling | CPU temperature sensors show high temps, CPU usage drops after a while. | Clean fans, improve airflow, check BIOS fan curves. | --- ## Monitoring over time (not just a snapshot) If you need to track CPU usage continuously: | Tool | Platform | How to use | |------|----------|------------| | **Windows Performance Monitor** (`perfmon`) | Windows | Add counters like `\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time`; export logs to CSV. | | **Grafana + Prometheus** | Cross‑platform | Install node_exporter on Linux/macOS; scrape metrics; visualize trends. | | **psutil (Python)** | Cross‑platform | `import psutil; psutil.cpu_percent(interval=1)`; loop to log values. | | **sysstat (sar)** | Linux | `sar -u 1 5` (sample every second, 5 times). | --- ## Quick sanity check ```powershell # PowerShell one‑liner to print overall CPU usage every 2 seconds, 5 samples Get-Counter '\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time' -SampleInterval 2 -MaxSamples 5 | Select-Object -ExpandProperty CounterSamples | Format-Table Timestamp, CookedValue ``` ```bash # Bash one‑liner (Linux) while read i; do echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') CPU: $i%"; sleep 2; done < <(watch -n 2 -d -t -q -x 'grep '^cpu ' /proc/stat | awk '{print ($2+$4)*100/($2+$4+$5)}') ``` *(The Bash snippet uses `/proc/stat` to compute CPU usage; adjust as needed.)* --- ### Bottom line * **CPU usage** tells you how busy your processor is. * Use the built‑in tools (Task Manager, Activity Monitor, top/htop) for quick checks. * For deeper diagnostics, look at per‑process stats, I/O wait, and thermal data. * If you see sustained spikes without an obvious reason, investigate background services, malware, or hardware issues. Feel free to let me know which OS you’re on or if you’d like a script to log CPU usage automatically!
